look_here_first: Start with the fruit: black walnut has by far the largest fruit in this trio, usually about 3.5–8 cm, and the nut surface between the deep grooves is coarsely warty. Mature trees can also become dramatically taller and heavier-trunked.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Detailed Williamson County treatment; contemporary Travis County riparian documentation; Burnet County local-species occurrence listing. Texas native status is confirmed by Kew/FNA.

best_field_traits: nut about 3–4 cm, deeply grooved with coarsely warty surface between grooves
dark deeply ridged bark on mature trees
morphology_keys.comparison_training: J. major has smaller 2–3.5 cm fruit with smoother nut surfaces between grooves; J. microcarpa has tiny fruit and many very narrow leaflets.

comparisons.key_distinctions: J. nigra is the large-fruited species; use the coarsely warty nut surface to confirm.

taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO. Flora of North America warns that central Texas intermediates occur among local walnut species; use multiple characters on atypical material.
